<!-- pr-reviewer: 39ffe9606ac51f1c5936df102d36de942070653a -->
Reviewer: MacBook-Pro.local pool job review-4170 (config ~/.claude-bob), claude-opus-5-5, mkinney; did not write or refresh this PR.

**Verdict: clean. No blockers.** This is a safety-tier review, because the PR changes posted G-code (`G64 P`).

### What looks good
- `tolP()` replaces each `"P" + fu(tol)` that can round to zero. The LinuxCNC header blend (`pathWords`) and the smoothing word (`smoothOn`) use it. The Tormach smoothing word uses it.
- I searched all posts for `G64 P`. The other writers (`tormach.cps` `blendP()`, `tormach-lathe.cps`, `tormach-plasma.cps`) write fixed positive values. No other post can write `G64 P0`.
- `fu()` and `trim()` are the same in the two posts. A value under the resolution gives `"0"`, and `tolP` then writes `P0.001` (mm) or `P0.0001` (inch). This is the first choice that #4147 gives.
- Smoothing on `Off` is not changed: `smoothOn` still returns when `smoothTol` is not above 0.
- The new tests join existing binaries (`linuxcnc_post`, `smoothing`). No new top-level test file.
- No recorded program (`*.nc`, `*.cl`, `examples/catalog/**`) changed. `conformance` and `example_catalog` are green, so no golden moved.
- The trial merge with upstream/main `e6849c5ae` was clean.

### Results (local, trial merge with upstream/main `e6849c5ae`)
- Quick gate (`cargo xtask gate quick --base upstream/main`): 103 steps, 0 failed, 0 stalled. This includes the post and app builds, `linuxcnc_post`, `smoothing`, `script_linuxcnc`, `script_tormach`, all `tormach_*` suites, `conformance` and `example_catalog`.
- Pinning tests: `linuxcnc_post::blend_tolerance_never_writes_g64_p0` and `smoothing::linuxcnc_and_tormach_smoothing_tolerance_never_writes_g64_p0` pass.
- Light lane (`cargo xtask gate light`, release): 6 steps, 0 failed.
- `cargo clippy -p camcraft-app --tests -- -D warnings`: clean.
- Heavy lanes: not run. This is a `P3` PR, and AGENTS.md "Heavy lanes at review" does not ask for them.

### Extra suites run
- `example_catalog` and `conformance` (posts changed): pass.
- No `testdata/` and no importer change, so no other extra suite applies.

### Mutations (each reverted after the run)
1. LinuxCNC `tolP` writes `"P" + s` with no clamp: `blend_tolerance_never_writes_g64_p0` is red (line 224), and the smoothing test is red for LinuxCNC (line 247).
2. Tormach `tolP` writes `"P" + s` with no clamp: the smoothing test is red for `Tormach PathPilot` (line 247).
3. LinuxCNC inch clamp writes `P0.001` instead of `P0.0001`: `blend_tolerance_never_writes_g64_p0` is red (line 224).

The tests catch each mutation.

### Optional, non-blocking
1. The fixing commit `39ffe9606` has no body. AGENTS.md "Pull Request Law" asks that its body ends with `Fixes #4147`. The PR body has `Fixes #4147`, so GitHub closes the issue on merge. Also, the PR body should end with `Fixes #4147` (now the `Changelog:` line comes after it), and it should say what was not exercised (for example: no run on a LinuxCNC or PathPilot control).
2. No test pins the Tormach smoothing clamp in inch (`P0.0001`). The code is the same as the LinuxCNC code, which the inch header test pins. A follow-up test is `P7`.
3. The clamp makes the written tolerance larger than the asked tolerance. For example, a 0.001 mm blend in an inch program writes `P0.0001` (0.00254 mm). #4147 permits this. A program note that says the tolerance was raised to the written resolution can help the operator. This is a suggestion only.
4. `s === "-0"` in `tolP` cannot be true: `trim()` already changes `"-0"` to `"0"`. The check does no harm.

@JSwetz, the review is clean. Please mark the PR ready (`gh pr ready 4170`) so that it can merge on this review. A maintainer will approve and merge by hand.
